title: HNB in Croatia’s inflation debate
subtitle: Media evidence for monetary communication
paper_title: Pasivno zamijenjena: cijena inflacije koju ne mjeri indeks potrošačkih cijena
paper_subtitle: Od inflacijskog vala do dezinflacije: institucionalni jaz u pažnji HNB-a 2021.–2026.
dataset_last_observed_day_status: Documented in the dataset README; later periods are not the headline analytical sample.
citation: Palić, P., & Sikić, L. (2026). Pasivno zamijenjena: cijena inflacije koju ne mjeri indeks potrošačkih cijena. Extended research draft, 17 September 2026. Hrvatsko katoličko sveučilište.
contributions: Both researchers are named as authors in the manuscript. Individual contribution roles are not specified.
question: How visible is the central bank when inflation dominates the news?
answer: The primary model associates higher inflation with lower weighted institutional visibility. Visibility also declines during April 2024–May 2026. A stable relationship with consumer expectations is not established.

findings.headline: Higher inflation is associated with lower visibility
findings.text: A 1 percentage-point higher HICP inflation rate is associated with a 0.21 percentage-point lower weighted share in the primary weekly model.
findings.caveat: The association is sensitive to time controls; it does not establish causality.
findings.implication: For HNB: the size of the inflation debate and the bank’s share of it answer different questions.

findings.headline: Visibility declines during April 2024–May 2026
findings.text: The weighted institutional share declines by 0.076 percentage points per month after accounting for inflation and the other regressors.
findings.caveat: This is a within-period association, not evidence that disinflation causes lower visibility.
findings.implication: For HNB: assess the coverage of monetary explanations even after the initial inflation surge has passed.

findings.headline: A stable link to expectations is not established
findings.text: Forward projections of consumer expectations depend on how monthly survey information is assigned to weeks and which controls are used. They do not robustly establish a persistent predictive channel.
findings.caveat: Some horizons are significant under other specifications. The survey balance does not measure long-term anchoring or trust.
findings.implication: For HNB: read media visibility alongside survey evidence; one cannot substitute for the other.
